rounds.hypothesis: Diagnose's invariant: socket(2) rejects on three axes, each owning a different errno, and once a family is recognized EAFNOSUPPORT must never be returned again. The four failures are not four bugs but one structural defect -- sys_socket inlines the whole family x type x protocol table into the syscall handler, so every rejection arm reaches for the same EAFNOSUPPORT regardless of which argument was at fault. Fixing the errno constants in place would leave the structure that produced them, and sys_socketpair's divergent copy of the same table untouched. So: hoist the table into a per-family dispatch under kernel/src/net/socket/ that both syscalls call, and let each family own its own axis order.
rounds.change: Added kernel/src/net/socket/create.rs with `new_socket`, `new_socket_pair`, and a private `resolve` that maps the triple to a `SocketKind` without constructing it. `resolve` gives each family its own arm with its own check order, measured from the host: AF_UNIX and AF_VSOCK check protocol before type (only wildcard 0 or the family's own number accepted, else EPROTONOSUPPORT); AF_INET/AF_INET6 check the protocol *range* first (outside 0..IPPROTO_MAX -> EINVAL), then type, then protocol; AF_NETLINK checks type before protocol, the opposite of UNIX. Unhandled-type-in-a-known-family now returns ESOCKTNOSUPPORT instead of falling through to the domain catch-all, and the four netlink arms return EPROTONOSUPPORT instead of EAFNOSUPPORT. Added an explicit IP SOCK_RAW arm returning EPROTONOSUPPORT (not EPERM: the host returns it to a fully privileged caller too). The outer catch-all keeps EAFNOSUPPORT, which is what still makes tdat[0] AF_UNSPEC pass. Added IPPROTO_MAX to kernel/src/util/net/socket.rs, derived from the Protocol enum's own highest variant. sys_socket and sys_socketpair now keep only their family-agnostic parts (type-range check, flag bits, fd installation); socketpair.rs's bogus `Protocol::try_from` on a value it never inspected is gone, and its EAFNOSUPPORT catch-all became EOPNOTSUPP, reached only after the triple is accepted.
rounds.outcome: green on the first run: socket01 9 passed / 0 failed / 0 broken, matching the host's 9/9 and diagnose's regression-guard target exactly. Two further boots on the same tree: (a) socket01,socket02,socketpair01,socketpair02,bind03,bind04,listen01,setsockopt03,sendmmsg02 -> 43 passed / 0 failed / 0 broken / 1 skipped (bind04 skips, as it does at base -- it is already enabled in all.txt on the CI path, so its skip is pre-existing and does not affect the aggregate line); (b) AUTO_TEST=regression -> 'All regression tests passed.', which is what exercises the *successful* creation paths through the new layer, including netlink ROUTE and KOBJECT_UEVENT over both SOCK_RAW and SOCK_DGRAM, AF_UNIX stream/dgram, AF_INET stream/dgram and AF_UNIX socketpair. Re-ran the target after the comment corrections below: socket01,socket02,socketpair01,socketpair02 -> 27 passed / 0 failed / 0 broken. cargo check, clippy and rustfmt are all clean, and `cargo rustdoc -D rustdoc::broken_intra_doc_links` passes. One self-correction inside the round: I had written Linux line-number anchors (af_unix.c#L1002, af_inet.c#L246, af_netlink.c#L664) into the doc comments, but diagnose recorded that every code host is blocked from this container and I confirmed elixir.bootlin.com still is, so those anchors were invented rather than read. Replaced them with file-and-function references I can actually stand behind.

layer: The per-family socket-creation dispatch, exactly the owning_layer diagnose named. It owns the invariant because the errno decision is a property of what a *family* implements, not of which syscall asked: the family knows whether it has a socket of that type and whether it implements that protocol, and nothing above it does. Placing it at the syscall entry point means one copy per entry point, which is not a hypothetical drift -- socket.rs and socketpair.rs already disagreed, and socketpair.rs additionally parsed a protocol it then ignored. The decisive evidence for this placement is black-box and needs no source read: on the host, socketpair(AF_INET, SOCK_RAW, 0) returns EPROTONOSUPPORT while socketpair(AF_INET, SOCK_STREAM, 0) returns EOPNOTSUPP. Same syscall, same family, different errnos, so the EPROTONOSUPPORT can only have come from a family-level create step that runs *before* the pair-specific operation is consulted. new_socket_pair reproduces exactly that order: resolve the triple first, then fail with EOPNOTSUPP only if the resolved socket cannot be made as a pair.
generalizes: The test walks 4 of the 22 rejection paths this change corrects, and it never supplies a protocol outside 0/1/6/17 nor any family but AF_UNSPEC/AF_UNIX/AF_INET. Each of diagnose's five other_callers is fixed by the shared layer rather than by a branch: (1) sys_socketpair no longer carries its own table -- it was wrong two ways (EAFNOSUPPORT where the host says EOPNOTSUPP for AF_INET stream/dgram pairs, and EPROTONOSUPPORT for AF_INET raw) and both now come out right; socketpair01, which was not the selected test and stays blocked this round, went green as a side effect, and its 10-row table independently checks EOPNOTSUPP, EPROTONOSUPPORT, EFAULT and the preserved EAFNOSUPPORT. (2) All four netlink rejection arms now return EPROTONOSUPPORT, matching the host for protocols 3, 31, 40 and -1 on a family Asterinas otherwise fully supports; AF_NETLINK+SOCK_STREAM now returns ESOCKTNOSUPPORT as the host does. (3) Recognized-family-with-unhandled-type (AF_INET+SOCK_RDM/SOCK_DCCP/SOCK_SEQPACKET, AF_UNIX+SOCK_RDM) returns ESOCKTNOSUPPORT instead of claiming the address family is unsupported. (4) An in-range but unassigned protocol (99 measured) now returns EPROTONOSUPPORT instead of EINVAL, while out-of-range values (263, 300, -1 measured) still return EINVAL -- the range boundary was measured, not assumed: 262 succeeds and 263 fails, so IPPROTO_MAX is 263, which is also one past the Protocol enum's highest variant, so the constant is derived from the enum instead of hardcoded. (5) AF_UNIX and AF_VSOCK now check their protocol argument, which they previously ignored entirely, so socket(AF_UNIX, SOCK_STREAM, 6) returns EPROTONOSUPPORT as on the host. Anti-overfitting checks I ran deliberately: no branch anywhere tests the specific values socket01 uses; every arm was written from a host measurement of the general rule, including 40 triples the test never touches. The one thing the test depends on that I had to actively preserve is the outer catch-all keeping EAFNOSUPPORT -- CSocketAddrFamily::AF_UNSPEC is a real enum variant, so try_from(0) succeeds and tdat[0] passes only because of that arm; flipping it to make the raw case pass would have traded one red row for another at 5/9. Where I did NOT generalize, and why: two combinations keep a technically-wrong errno because they are missing features rather than errno defects, and diagnose scoped them out. AF_INET6+SOCK_DGRAM keeps EAFNOSUPPORT (the host creates a UDPv6 socket; Asterinas's DatagramSocket is IPv4-only, so the family is only half-implemented, and EAFNOSUPPORT is the answer userspace already treats as 'no IPv6 here, fall back' -- changing it to ESOCKTNOSUPPORT would swap one wrong answer for a less idiomatic one and risk currently-green tests). AF_VSOCK datagram/seqpacket and IP raw sockets are likewise unimplemented. All three carry TODOs naming the feature rather than silently entrenching the conflation.
fix_summary: Moves the (family, type, protocol) -> socket decision out of the two syscall handlers into one per-family dispatch, kernel/src/net/socket/create.rs, and gives each rejection axis its own errno: EAFNOSUPPORT only while the family is still unrecognized, ESOCKTNOSUPPORT for a known family with no socket of that type, EPROTONOSUPPORT for a known family and type that does not implement the protocol (including wildcard 0 with no default to resolve to), and EINVAL only for a protocol number outside the valid range. Designed against Asterinas's own abstractions rather than transplanted from Linux: Linux hangs this off a registered net_proto_family::create function pointer, but Asterinas has no family registry -- each socket is a plain Rust type with an inherent constructor -- so instead of inventing a vtable, `resolve` returns a `SocketKind` value that names the socket without building it. That is what lets the two callers share every check and still differ in what they construct: new_socket builds one socket from the SocketKind, new_socket_pair matches the same SocketKind and builds a connected pair, returning EOPNOTSUPP for the kinds that have no pair form -- which also reproduces Linux's observable ordering, where socketpair's family/type/protocol errors precede its EOPNOTSUPP. The syscall handlers keep only what is genuinely family-agnostic: the SockType range check, the SOCK_NONBLOCK/SOCK_CLOEXEC flag bits, and fd installation.
